sources.source_name: Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project — overview PDF
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Inspected PDF text; states 81 books (46 OT, 35 NT), distinguishes narrower/broader canon, lists titles. Not proof of official endorsement, full English text, completeness, or reuse rights.

sources.source_name: Ethiopian Bible — 81-book canon list
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Inspected canon/count discussion. Provides a working secondary enumeration, explains composite count variations, and warns 81/88 counts vary by grouping. Not a universally authoritative church-issued enumeration or a text license.
sources.archive_status: External source only; specialist review needed

sources.source_name: English availability audit
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Reports no complete English translation and identifies rare/untranslated texts. Treat as a research lead; independently verify book by book.

sources.source_name: Free text and legal downloads guide
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Identifies candidate public-domain translations: Charles Enoch (1912), Charles Jubilees (1902), KJV Apocrypha / Brenton for some deuterocanonical books. Verify exact edition, completeness, jurisdiction and rights.

sources.source_name: Free English online reader
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Inspected page description: offers seven books/selection, not all 81/88. Identifies some underlying translation families but not comprehensive availability.

sources.source_name: Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library (IAA)
sources.inspection_and_limitations: IAA repository description confirms public digital manuscript-image access. Confirm image-specific terms and exact identifiers before reuse.

sources.source_name: 11Q11 transcription
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Inspected Hebrew fragment transcription; brackets mark editorial restoration. Not a complete “Secret Book of Solomon”; compare to scholarly editions.

sources.source_name: Oxford Handbook of Psalms — apocryphal Qumran psalms
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Scholarly excerpt describes 11Q11 as damaged, with exorcistic material and Psalm 91. Full chapter access/reuse not established.

sources.source_name: British Library Askew Codex catalogue
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Catalogue identifies Pistis Sophia / Askew Codex as Coptic Add MS 5114, 178 folios; images reported unavailable in this result. Not part of the baseline canon catalogue.

sources.source_name: Pistis Sophia older English translation
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Mead translation text is readable online; translation edition and redistribution rights need separate review.

sources.source_name: Testament of Solomon — Internet Archive item supplied by user
sources.inspection_and_limitations: URL supplied by user; the research browser could not open it. Edition, contents, access, and rights remain unchecked. It is separate from 11Q11 and not in baseline canon list.

sources.source_name: Testament of Solomon — Early Jewish Writings
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Secondary overview describes a pseudepigraphical Solomon work; composition/date are debated. Not a primary manuscript or canon authority.

sources.source_name: Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project — English books category
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Inspected category. Lists a newly announced English 3 Meqabyan edition translated from Amharic with comparison to earlier English witnesses; the post directs readers to a commercial edition. Translation provenance and reuse rights require direct verification. Site is a project, not evidence of official church approval.

sources.source_name: Digital Ark
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Opened the supplied candidate site, but page content was unavailable to the research browser in this review. Search description advertises an 81-book online Bible; no text, completeness, source metadata, or license was inspected.

sources.source_name: Project Gutenberg
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Inspected general library home page, which says it focuses on older works whose US copyright has expired. No individual Ethiopian-canon text record was checked here.
sources.archive_status: Repository lead; item-level search and license check needed

sources.source_name: Ethiopian Bible sources and editorial standards
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Inspected statements on source hierarchy, public-domain translations, unresolved book-count conventions, and nine books with no widely available English translation. Secondary source; confirm against church and academic sources.

sources.source_name: Ertale Bible sources
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Request returned HTTP 403 in this review; page contents and source citations were not inspected.

sources.source_name: Louvre collection record — Baal Cycle tablet AO 16643 / RS 3.361
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Primary museum catalogue identifies an incomplete inscribed clay tablet found at Ras Shamra, dated broadly to Late Bronze Age II, and classifies its text as a Baal Cycle myth. One artifact record does not establish location/access for every Cycle tablet.

sources.source_name: French Ministry of Culture — Baal Cycle at Ugarit
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Institutional archaeology overview of the Baal Cycle and Ugarit/Ras Shamra; use for context, not as a complete critically edited text.

sources.source_name: John C. L. Gibson, Ugaritic Literary Texts (Brill chapter excerpt)
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Scholarly excerpt identifies the Baal myth as KTU 1.1–1.6, describes its tablet witnesses and the scribe Ilimilku. The full critical translation/commentary cited in the excerpt is a separate edition.
sources.archive_status: Scholarly reference; edition rights not assessed

sources.source_name: Ugaritic Myths, Epics, and Legends — Marquette University resource
sources.inspection_and_limitations: University-hosted PDF containing translations/discussion of Ugaritic myths. Exact Baal Cycle coverage, edition metadata and reuse rights need item-level review before republication.

sources.source_name: User-provided Baal Cycle excerpt — ANET page 137
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Identified from the supplied scan by matching its wording to “Poems about Baal and Anath (The Baal Cycle),” in James B. Pritchard (ed.), Ancient Near Eastern Texts Relating to the Old Testament, 3rd ed. with supplement (Princeton University Press, 1969), section “Ugaritic Myths, Epics, and Legends,” p. 137; translation attributed to Harold L. Ginsberg. The supplied image was not copied into the site. This is a copyrighted anthology translation; online reproduction rights are unresolved.
sources.archive_status: User image identified; bibliographic record; do not reproduce without rights clearance

sources.source_name: USCCB — Daniel 7
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Primary biblical chapter and study notes used for the Daniel 7 beast-imagery comparison. Translation and theological framing belong to the cited edition.

sources.source_name: USCCB — Revelation 13
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Primary biblical chapter and study notes used for the Revelation 13 sea-beast comparison. Translation and theological framing belong to the cited edition.

sources.source_name: University of Denver thesis — Baal Cycle discussion
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Secondary overview of KTU 1.5–1.6 covering Anat’s treatment of Mot, Baal’s return, the seven-year interval, and the final confrontation. Seasonal-cycle language is scholarly interpretation, not presented as a direct statement from the tablets.

sources.source_name: USCCB — 2 Kings 1 and Baal-zebub note
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Primary biblical chapter. The accompanying note describes Baal-zebub as a derisive alteration of Baal-zebul (“Prince Baal”) and says the best New Testament evidence supports Beelzebul. This is a translation/commentary position; name history is debated.

sources.source_name: USCCB — Synoptic Beelzebul passages
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Mark 3:22 reports the Beelzebul accusation; see Matthew 12:24–29 and Luke 11:14–23 for parallels. The Gospel passages frame Beelzebul as “prince of demons.”

sources.source_name: “The Devil in the Details: Beelzebul and Social Identity Complexity in Mark 3:20–35”
sources.inspection_and_limitations: Peer-reviewed article surveys competing proposals for the name Beelzebul, including a Baal-related origin, and argues for a likely derivation from the Ekron deity name. Treat the etymology as debated, not settled.

related_texts.title: The Ugaritic Baal Cycle
related_texts.not_canonical_note: Not part of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo biblical canon. Included for comparative study only.
related_texts.description: A fragmentary Ugaritic mythological poem preserved on six tablet units, conventionally catalogued as KTU 1.1–1.6. The tablets were found at Ras Shamra (ancient Ugarit); the Louvre catalogue documents individual tablet witnesses, including AO 16643 / RS 3.361. The user-provided excerpt is identified as a 1969 ANET translation on page 137. Exact ordering, restoration and translation are scholarly matters.
related_texts.text_status: External sources identified; no text reproduced

related_texts.title: Pistis Sophia
related_texts.also_known_as: Askew Codex; British Library Add MS 5114
related_texts.not_canonical_note: Not part of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo biblical canon and not a Dead Sea Scroll.
related_texts.description: A Coptic manuscript held by the British Library. Catalogue record identifies Add MS 5114; images were marked unavailable in the inspected catalogue result.
related_texts.text_status: Catalogue metadata and an older English text lead identified

related_texts.title: Testament of Solomon
related_texts.not_canonical_note: Separate from 11Q11; not treated as part of the Ethiopian canon here.
related_texts.description: A work attributed to Solomon in later literary tradition. Its composition and dating are debated. The user-provided Internet Archive item is an unverified edition lead.

related_texts.title: 11Q11 — Apocryphal Psalms
related_texts.not_canonical_note: A fragmentary Qumran manuscript, not a standalone Solomon book. It preserves exorcistic psalm material and Psalm 91; Solomon appears in a damaged passage.
